title: Revoking a device voids its unused authority; completed effects and history stay; a suspected compromise opens a review
statement: My preferred policy is that revoking a device should immediately invalidate its unused authority to authorize future execution. Actions already legitimately completed must remain in the evidence ledger. Revocation must not erase history or pretend an external effect never happened. A suspected key compromise should trigger a separate retrospective integrity review. Distinguish historical validity of a signature from its continuing authority to approve a new effect. Develop and test that policy in the sandbox, but keep constitutional changes subject to the existing authenticated founder-approval process. Do not silently alter protected authority rules.
exact_source_excerpt: revoking a device should immediately invalidate its unused authority to authorize future execution
changed_axis: authority (CLAUDE.md developmental-inheritance axes): how long a delegated device key's answer keeps authorizing. It narrows; nothing is widened. The delegation itself (DEVICE_KINDS, the founder-key-only kinds, the 90-day limit) is unchanged.
intended_effect: After the founder revokes a device key, nothing that key approved and that has not yet been used lets GREG start a new effect, an observation outside the mission's scope included. The mission asks again. Everything already done under the key keeps its record and its receipt. When the founder suspects the key was compromised, one list of everything it signed and everything that rested on it is put in front of the founder.
executable_interpretation: The mission fold (greg/missions.py MissionBook._revoked) voids, at the ledger position of a device.revoked record, every answer that key signed that still authorizes something not yet done: an approve of an ask whose scope the Gate honours (APPROVAL: a standing exact scope or a paid run not yet made; SENSOR_SCOPE: a standing out-of-cone observation) and a reconcile_* answer the engine has not recorded. The request counts as withdrawn and is asked again under a new request id. Rejections and record-only answers are not voided; every ask kind in greg/ is in exactly one class, pinned by a test. greg/revocation.py writes the trail (one decision.withdrawn per voided answer, naming the device, the revocation and the answer) and, for DEVICE_REVOKE with suspected_compromise: true (signed with the revocation, or later for the revoked key), one device.integrity_review record and one DEVICE_INTEGRITY_REVIEW ask that only the founder key answers. The separate appraiser (greg/appraisal.py) refutes a closure whose action was dispatched after the revocation on the revoked key's approval. Fix round 2026-11-12, after an independent review: a mission the revoked key's own LIFECYCLE command ended stays ended, and its compensations the Gate had not dispatched are held by the fold (MissionState.compensation_hold) until an approval of each one's exact scope; a compensation the Gate dispatched before the revocation is recorded from the Gate's own record; the review attributes to the key only the dispatches granted while its approval stood.
owner: Alfonso Lopez (founder authority); the implementing session on branch claude/revoked-device-authority-20261111
authority_level: active_requirement; implemented as a sandbox draft for founder review
binding_scope: greg/ only: the mission fold, the body's DEVICE_REVOKE command, the founder-ask surfaces and the separate appraiser. Reversible implementation, tests and a local branch. No merge, push, deployment, spending, credential or outside-contact authority. No protected artifact (governance/integrity/manifest.json) is touched.
constitutional_constraints: Chat text is intent evidence, not founder authentication; it authorizes no runtime act
No constitution, authority matrix, identity file or policy/consequence_gate.py is changed; python -m governance.integrity --check stays clean
A device key stays a delegation, never a second founder: this change removes authority from a revoked device and gives none to anyone
History is append-only: the device's answers, their commands and every receipt stay on the ledger, and the ledger still verifies
success_evidence: tests/unit/test_greg_revoked_device_authority.py on real bodies: copied unchanged onto the integration head 8d205324, 42 of its 50 tests fail (the reproduction on the assertion that the write did not run) and 8 pass
scripts/ci/check_revoked_device_mutants.py: each safeguard removed in a scratch copy fails a behavioral test
A device-approved write that completed before the revocation is still VERIFIED by the separate appraiser after it
tests/unit/test_greg_revoked_device_review.py on real bodies: the four findings of the independent review of f35b7986, each reproduced before it was changed, and the mutants that review found alive
failure_evidence: An action, compensation or observation dispatched after a device.revoked record on an approval that key signed
A receipt, action record or answer changed or removed by a revocation
A review that revokes or rewrites anything, or that a device key can close
dependencies: greg/founder.py DEVICE_KINDS and FounderVerifier (a revoked key signs nothing; a re-delegated key verifies only later tokens)
greg/recovery.py and greg/autonomy.py (the existing decision.withdrawn voids_approval precedent this reuses)
conflicts: greg/goal_gravity.py APPROVE_MEANS says an unpaid approve stands for the mission's lifetime until the mission closes or its horizon passes. Narrowed here: it also ends when the device key that signed it is revoked. The founder's own approvals are unchanged.

The brief for this work says draft #290 records this as an open gap (a DECISION a device signed before its revocation still counts). The finishing session did not find that sentence in #290's tree (facea170) and did not read the pull request page; the gap itself is reproduced by the first test. Wherever #290 records it, that text is not edited from this branch.
next_review_trigger: Founder review of the draft and of the fourteen open questions in ADR-20261111 (above all: whether what a revoked device resumed should be paused again, and whether the compensations of a mission it ended are rightly held); a second independent review, of the fix round; the first revocation on a founder-device body
supersedes: The behaviour in which an answer a device signed kept authorizing new actions after the device was revoked
authority_delta: narrowing only: a revoked device's unused answers stop authorizing; nothing gains authority
